claims.text: The magnitude of local lattice distortion arising from atomic size mismatch controls dislocation glide resistance in refractory HEAs.
The magnitude of local lattice distortion controls the thermoelastic response of refractory HEAs.
Increasing local lattice distortion increases yield stress by enhancing dislocation pinning.
Increasing local lattice distortion alters temperature-dependent elastic moduli through changes in vibrational dynamics.
HfNbTaTiZr is an example of a BCC-structured refractory HEA.
Targeted substitution with an element having a sufficiently different atomic radius can increase atomic size mismatch and local lattice distortion.
Mean-square atomic displacement can quantify the relevant local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions create a heterogeneous dislocation glide-resistance landscape.
Local distortions generate fluctuating internal stress fields that impede dislocation motion through solid-solution strengthening.
Local lattice distortions alter vibrational modes that determine thermoelastic moduli.
Sluggish diffusion is typical of refractory HEAs under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Sluggish diffusion sustains local barriers to dislocation motion at high temperature.
Relative to a low-mismatch baseline, a high-distortion alloy will have a clearly elevated high-temperature yield strength.
Relative to the baseline, a high-distortion alloy will exhibit a distinct temperature dependence of elastic modulus, potentially including reduced softening or anomalous stiffening.
The high-distortion alloy may show dynamic solute pinning manifested as serrated flow.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply to single-phase, compositionally uniform refractory HEAs tested from 600°C to 1200°C in inert atmospheres.
Multiphase microstructures, oxidation, grain size, texture, and defect distributions may alter the predicted relationships.
